title: Stop Doing scale trends Wrong: Train Your weekly averages Instead
description: Stop letting single mornings steer your gaining. Weigh through the test, learn to train your weekly averages like a skill, and hand the steering wheel to the only scale number that tells the truth.

scenes.narration: Stop doing the scale wrong. | Seven mornings, this week. | Same time, same routine. | Write every number down. | Average all seven now. | That average is your truth. | Compare last week's average. | The difference is your trend. | Second, max strict push-ups. | Floor to lockout, clean. | Count the honest reps. | That is your second number. | Keep the pair together. | At the end I tell | you how to train averages | like any other skill. | Single mornings have been steering | your gaining, and single mornings | lie with complete confidence. | Today we retire them from | every decision. | Weigh like a scientist.

scenes.label: AVERAGES ARE A TRAINABLE SKILL, NOT A TALENT
scenes.sub: daily verdicts: noise steering - weekly averages: tissue steering
scenes.narration: Here is the reframe this episode installs: the weekly average is not a statistic you glance at. It is a skill you train, with a technique, a progression, and a maintenance phase, exactly like a pull-up. The untrained version looks like this: sporadic weigh-ins, emotional readings, decisions made on single mornings, and a trend that exists only as a feeling. The trained version: a fixed ritual, an unbroken record, a Sunday computation, and decisions made monthly in small steps. Same scale, same body, opposite information. Men are not bad at reading their weight. They are untrained at it, and untrained is the most fixable condition on this channel. Your push-up number, by the way, is the average's partner instrument, and today we train them as a pair.

Train the average the way it actually works. Each morning's number is a sample contaminated by water, glycogen, gut contents, and sleep. The contamination is random, the tissue change is directional, and averaging across seven samples is the filter that separates them. But the filter has operating conditions, and training the average means honoring them: samples taken under identical conditions, none deleted, none repeated because the first reading displeased you. A re-weigh is the original sin of this instrument, the moment the scientist becomes a negotiator. The mechanism also sets the decision tempo: because the filter needs a week to clean the signal and two weeks to confirm a change, your decisions inherit that tempo. Slow instrument, slow decisions, fast results across a season. The re-weigh deserves its full sentence of shame: stepping off and on again to negotiate a kinder number teaches the scientist to distrust his own instrument and teaches the instrument nothing. Record the first number, especially when it stings. The sting is frequently the signal.

The science of trained measurement is the science of feedback loops. Studies of regular self-weighing find the benefit lives in the loop: measure, interpret calmly, adjust slightly, measure again. Break any link and the benefit dies; measure without calm interpretation and you get anxiety, interpret without measurement and you get folklore, adjust without patience and you get oscillation. The trained average strengthens every link at once. It also exploits a quirk of human motivation worth knowing: a visible, gently rising trend is one of the most reinforcing sights in a long project, more durable than motivation because it is evidence. Men do not quit programs whose dashboards show honest progress. They quit programs whose dashboards show weather and call it failure. The loop has a final link the folklore never mentions: the record itself becomes motivation's replacement. Six months of honest averages, rising in their band, will carry a man through the month his enthusiasm dies, because evidence does not need to feel like anything to keep working.

The progression of this skill, for the man installing it: week one is collection only, weigh and record with no interpretation allowed, because the first skill is attendance. Weeks two and three add the Sunday average and the comparison, still with no decisions, because the second skill is watching without flinching. Week four adds the first decision right, exercised only if the two-week signal demands it, in the smallest step the surplus system allows. Maintenance, from month two onward, is a monthly review where the average and a strength test are read together like a lab report. Notice the shape: it is the same progression as learning a muscle-up, scaled down to a bathroom floor. Capacity first, judgment later, decisions last.

Your advantage in training this skill is that your signal is the cleanest in the building. Your water swings are modest, your tissue trend is the whole story, and your corrections are snack-sized, so the loop can run at its gentlest setting and still steer perfectly. The dieter trains this skill against a body actively resisting him, with rebound water forging his data weekly. You train it in a quiet lab. There is a final advantage, the one that compounds across this whole season: a man with a trained average never needs to ask the internet whether he is gaining. He owns the instrument, the record, and the answer. Independence is the real product here. The muscle is almost a side effect.

Train the partner instrument with me. Four rounds of push-ups, forty seconds on, twenty off, counted with a scientist's honesty. No generous reps. The average and the test are read together, so both must deserve trust.

The average-training protocol, four rules. One: fix the collection ritual permanently, same scale, same spot, same morning moment, and treat a missed morning as a missing sample, never a disaster. Two: compute every Sunday, compare every second Sunday, and decide only at the monthly review, so the tempo of decisions matches the tempo of tissue. Three: pair every monthly decision with the same strength test, because mass without performance is a rumor. Four: keep the record forever, in one place, because the season-long trend is the biography this whole project is writing. Follow these and the scale stops being a mood with batteries. It becomes the lab instrument your gaining always needed.

Your verdict, the pair read together. A rising average in the honest band with modest push-ups: the instrument says the climate is right and the engine is next, so train while the dashboard watches. A flat average for a month with any push-ups: the instrument has earned the right to be believed, so make the one small addition it prescribes. A falling average during a bulk: the bravest reading of all, and the answer is food, promptly, without debating the messenger. A rising average and climbing push-ups: the loop is closed and working, and your only duty is to keep collecting. Comment your weekly change and your push-up number. In thirty days, bring four more averages, and we will read the season together. And if your average today contradicted a story you loved about your gaining, keep the average. Stories are revised in an afternoon. Records, kept honestly, revise themselves into the truth across a season.

Thirty days from now, same scale, same ritual, same push-up test. Bring me a trained average and a bigger number. Subscribe, and let the record grow unbroken until then. This is {channel}. Train the cable.
